newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares edge up, seen stabilising.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares edge up, seen stabilising.

text.p: Polish shares edged up in lower turnover on Monday and analysts said they were likely to stay flat this week and probably next in the absence of signals that would push the market from its horizontal trend.
The main market's WIG index rose 0.1 percent to 14,744.0 points and turnover fell 10.3 percent to 124.2 million zlotys ($44.4 million) on both markets as 35 issues rose, 26 fell and 17 were flat.

"The market doesn't know which way to go lacking strong signals and being close to the main market's (September 18) 14,832-point maximum and the psychological barrier of 15,000 points," said Mateusz Andrzejewski of Bank Pekao SA brokerage.

He said the market was likely to swing between 14,500 and 14,800 points until new signals appeared such as inflation data for September and companies' September earnings reports, both due in mid-October.
Analysts said if the reports proved good they could push the market to new highs and start a new growth trend.
But some analysts feared a profit-taking downtrend pulling the market down to about 12,500 points before year-end.

Analysts said biggest main-market loser garment maker Bytom fell 7.1 to 28.8 zlotys ($10) after the company set its new issue price at 27 zlotys ($9.6), but said the 0.2-million-zloty ($0.1 million) turnover suggested the fall might also have been accidental.
Mass privatisation NFI units rose 3.8 percent in a 14.1-million-zloty ($5.0 million) turnover in the regular bourse session but fell 0.7 percent in 14.6-million-zloty ($5.2 million) continuous trade.
Continuous trade turnover was at 2.3 million zlotys ($0.8 million) with biggest mover tyre maker Debica SA falling 1.6 percent.
